chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Mu'awiya, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who gives a loan in animals and food, and pledges a pledge. He said, 'There is no harm; you secure what is from your wealth.'

key_terms.إِسْلَامٌ: Giving a loan (specifically of consumable goods)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on pledging animals or food as security for a loan?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on pledges (*Rahn*), this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of using consumable goods like animals and food as collateral. The Imam’s ruling that one may 'secure from your wealth' (*tastawsiqu min malika*) establishes that the lender retains the right to recover the value of the pledged consumables from the borrower’s general assets, ensuring financial security in such transactions.
